title: Leyendecker in Paris
content: J.C. Leyendecker, during his student days in Paris, wrote home to Chicago describing the work he was doing in theAcadémie Julianunder Benjamin-Constant, Lefebvre, Bouguereau, and Laurens:"Thoroughness is the principle upon which the French Art Schools have won their success. It doesn't take long to discover that style and dash will not make a drawing or painting go here as it will an illustration back home. Serious work—getting right down to the foundation principles—is the demand which is laid upon every student over here.If I learned anything it was that a picture is really only valuable for the thought behind it. There is little talk of 'handling' and of the catch tricks of the trade, and much emphasis upon a deep and serious significance in everything attempted."More on Substack
